chunks: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā narrated from ʿAlī ibn Aḥmad ibn Ashyam, from Ṣafwān ibn Yaḥyā and Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn Abī Naṣr, who said:

We asked him about combining in tawaf between two circuits of seven and three. He said: No; it is only one set of seven and two rakʿahs. And he said: My father used to perform tawaf with Muḥammad ibn Ibrāhīm and would combine, but that was only from him due to the circumstance of taqiyyah.

key_terms.أُسْبُوعٌ: one complete set of seven circuits in tawaf
key_terms.التَّقِيَّةِ: dissimulation or precautionary conformity due to circumstances of risk or pressure
key_terms.الطَّوَافِ: the ritual circumambulation of the Kaʿbah
key_terms.الْقِرَانِ: combining multiple tawaf rounds together without separating them as prescribed
key_terms.رَكْعَتَانِ: the two rakʿahs performed after tawaf
key_terms.فَيَقْرُنُ: he would combine one tawaf with another

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to combine multiple tawaf rounds together, and was this ever done by the Imams عليهم السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling regarding tawaf, stating that one should not combine multiple rounds together in the manner asked about, but rather perform one seven-circuit tawaf followed by two rakʿahs. It also explains that an instance of combining attributed to the Imam’s father was done specifically under taqiyyah, indicating an outward practice adopted due to circumstances.
